Friends can text home, check the weather and look things up through your phone when it has signal — up to %1$d MB of your data a day.
Friends can text home, check the weather and look things up through your phone when it has signal — with no daily limit.

Phones in your group link to each other directly over Bluetooth and WiFi — no tower, no router, no internet.

Every message is signed with your group's code and passed from phone to phone, so it can travel down a line of hikers or across a crowd, far beyond one phone's range.

Every phone keeps the group's messages for 48 hours and fills in anyone who was away. Walk off, come back — the chat catches up on its own.

The ticks never lie: ◷ waiting for a phone in range, ✓ on its way, ✓✓ phones confirmed. Tap your own message to see exactly who has it.

Direct chats only show up on your screen and theirs — but they are not encrypted. Like everything else, they are passed along by the group's phones on the way, so someone with the group code and a modified app could read them.

Names aren't checked: anyone with the code can call themselves anything. When two people share a name, Hopline adds a short tag to tell them apart.

Anyone with the 3-word code can read the group, so treat it like a walkie-talkie, not a vault.
